tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Robert Brünauer in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab: 4. X. Brahms op. 119 No 1 Bild; Urlinie des Paisiello-Themas Beethoven.Schenker’s diary for Sept 28 records his sending out the “lesson table” to Brünauer and Elias.
7. Fingersatz u. Spiel bei Brahms u. Paisiello Thema u. Var. 1.Diary October 7: “Dr. Brünauer asks if he may bring his fee in two halves; would we receive his lady friend?”
25. Die Variationen zuende.Diary Oct 23: “In the evening, I work on Brahms's Op. 119, No. 2, for Brünauer.”

4. XI.
Beethoven: Eroica-Variationen, neu, Bild des Themas.Diary Nov 4: “Brünauer pays half his fee, in notes of different denominations, among them even silver shillings!!”
8. Brahms, op. 119 No 2, Bild begonnen.
25. Eroica-Variationen abgeschlossen.
29. Die Fuge begonnen.
2. XII. Einiges zum Forellen-Quintett.
6. Bild der Fuge.

9. Fingersatz.Diary Dec 9: “Dr. Brünauer speaks about wanting to acquire a Bechstein piano – I get furious, as I relate this acquisition to his lady friend: to pay me the lesson fees in half-installments, and in addition to make such a great expenditure: that is truly shameless!”

13. Nur Bassbrechungen der Fuge vorgeführt.Diary Dec 12: “The fugue from the "Eroica" Variations newly written out, in ink (for Dr. Brünauer)”. — Diary Dec 15: “Dr. Brünauer asked, via his messenger, whether he could come tomorrow at 5:30, or some other time – this petty bourgeois takes no notice of the previous [pupil], and asserts his right that I can give up my time for sake of his laziness – the repulsive instinct of a person who does not have a drop of decency in his blood.”
20. Einiges zu Weingartners Instrumentierung von op. 106.
23. Beethoven abgeschlossen.
27. Falstaff-Variationen, neu (Bilder).
30. Beide Hefte Liebeslieder-WalzerBrahms’s Liebeslieder, Op.52a and Neue Liebeslieder, Op. 65a. gespielt.

3. I. Ueber den Fingersatz einer Stelle in der Esm-Variation.The fourteenth of the “Eroica” Variations is in E minor, so Schenker is probably referring to that, not the fifth variation of WoO73, which is set in B minor.
13. Falstaff-Variationen abgeschlossen.

17. Bericht über das Furtwängler-Konzert.Concert on January 16 in the Great Hall of the Musikverein Building with the Vienna Philharmonic under Wilhelm Furtwängler, the program comprising Mendelssohn’s Third Symphony (“Scottish”) and Brahms’s Second Symphony.
20. Berçeuse wiederholt, neu: Linie.
3. II. Impromptu Asdur, neu, Linie.Diary Feb 3: “Dr. Brünauer pays for the entire month.” — Diary Feb 4: “In the morning, [...] I work on Chopin's Op. 29 (Impromptu), for Dr. Brünauer.”
7. Impromptu zuende.
10. Das Bild aller Variationen der Berçeuse selbst zuhause geschrieben.

17. Wiederholung der Noc-
-turne Fisdur.
21. Impromptu Fisdur, neu.Diary Feb 20: “I work on Chopin's Impromptu in F major (for Brünauer).”
24. Bild-Korrekturen.
28. Fingersatz.
21. III. Wiederholt Brahms Rhapsodie Hmoll (Bilder).

28. Unterbrechung durch Prof. Altmann.Diary March 28: “I work on the Urlinie of Brahms's Rhapsody in B minor (for Brünauer) [...] From 6:45 until 7:30, Director Altmann (I send Dr. Brünauer away).” – Diary May 14: “Brünauer receives the lesson that had been cancelled on account of Prof. Altmann's visit: four-hand music by Schumann (new) and Haydn.”

31. Ueber das Philharmonische Konzert der Beethoven-Feier.A concert in the Theater an der Wien, marking the centennial of Beethoven’s death, took place on March 27 at 11 a.m.: Program: Fifth Symphony, Violin Concerto, Third Piano Concerto, the Vienna Philharmonic conducted by Martin Spörr, with Hugo Gottesmann and Guido Peters as soloists. That evening, Goethe’s Egmont, with all of Beethoven’s incidental music, was staged at the Staatsoper, with the Vienna Philharmonic under Weingartner and the Klärchen songs sung by Lotte Lehmann.
4. IV. Insbesondere die Coda der Rhapsodie Hmoll.
7. Das 1. Thema aus dem Beethoven-Trio op. 97; neu: Nocturne Esdur op. 9.
21. Nocturne zuende.
28. Vierhändig eine Sinfonie von Haydn, Bd. III, die ich mit Vrieslander gespielt habe.
2. V. Vierhändig aus Schumanns Original-Stücken.
7. Haydn Fantasie gelesen u. eine Sinfonie vierhändig gespielt.
12. Einige Bassmodelle; aus der Nocturne Haydn fortgesetzt.
16. Modelle einzelner Stellen aus der Nocturne Fisdur, Esdur u. aus der Rhapsodie Hmoll zur Befestigung.

2. VI. Zu Haydns Fmoll-Andante
selbständig die Linie dargestellt, sehr gut.Diary June 2: “Mrs. Pairamall and Brünauer pay 50 shillings per lesson!!!”

9. Linie zu Mendelssohns Frühlingslied in der Stunde versucht.Diary June 9: “Work on the Urlinie of the Brahms Rhapsody (for Brünauer).” – Diary June 10: “Urlinie to Mendelssohn's ‘Spring Song’ (for Brünauer) and for Chopin's Prelude in D major (for Elias).”
13. Die neuen Händel-Funde aus der „Musik“ gezeigt; das Cmoll-Stück als von Bach befunden; flüchtiges Durchspielen von Mendelssohn Frühlingslied u. Hmoll-Stück.
15. Ueber die Nebennotenbewegung, genaue Bilder, namentlich Beispiele aus der Polonaise Cismoll.Diary June 15: “Brünauer from 5 to 6, a substitute lesson.”
20. Ueber das Variationen-Thema in Mozarts Sonate Ddur (vgl. Albersheim).Albersheim’s lesson for June 17: “the Urlinie of the D major theme from the D major sonata; on ornaments and their execution.”

tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Robert Brünauer in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab: October 7: Fingering and playing for the Brahms, and for the Paisiello theme and first variation.
October 25: The variations finished.

November 4:
Beethoven: “Eroica” Variations, new, graph of the theme.
November 8: Brahms, Op. 119, No. 2, graph begun.
November 25: “Eroica” Variations completed.
November 29: The fugue begun.
December 2: A few things about the “Trout” Quintet.
December 6: Graph of the fugue.
December 9: Fingering of the fugue.
December 13: Only the bass arpeggiations in the fugue presented.
December 20: Some things about Weingartner’s orchestration of Op. 106.
December 23: Beethoven completed.
December 27: “Falstaff” Variations, new (graphs).
December 30: The two volumes of Liebeslieder waltzes played.
January 3:Concerning the fingering of a passage in the E minor variation.
January 13: “Falstaff” Variations completed.
January 17: Report of the Furtwängler concert.
January 20: Berceuse revisited, new: voice-leading line
February 3: Impromptu in A major, new, voice-leading line.
February 7: Impromptu, Op. 29 finished.
February 10: The graph of all the variations of the Berceuse written by himself at home.

February 17: Revisiting of the
Nocturne in F major.
February 21: Impromptu in F major, new.
February 24: Corrections to the graph.
February 28: Fingering.
March 21: Revisiting of Brahms’s Rhapsody in B minor (graphs).
March 28: Interruption by Prof. Altmann.
March 31: About the Philharmonic concert at the Beethoven festival.
April 4: In particular, the coda of the Rhapsody in B minor.
April 7: The first theme from Beethoven’s Trio, Op. 97; new: Nocturne in E major from Op. 9.
April 21.: Nocturne finished.
April 28:A Symphony by Haydn from vol. III, which I played four-hands with Vrieslander.
May 2:Original piano-four-hand music by Schumann.
May 7: Haydn’s Fantasy read, and a symphony played four-hands.
May 12: A few bass models; Haydn continued.
May 16: Models for a few passages from the Nocturnes in F major and E major, and from the Rhapsody in B minor, for consolidation.

June 2: The voice-leading line of Haydn’s Andante in F minor
presented on his own, very good.
June 9: An attempt made in the lesson of the voice-leading line of Mendelssohn’s “Spring Song.”
June 15: On neighbor-note motion, precise graphs, in particular, examples from the Polonaise in C minor.
June 20: On the variation theme from Mozart’s Sonata in D major (cf. Albersheim).

tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Angi Elias in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab: 4. X. Brahms op. 119 No 1, Linie begonnen
7. Jöde; Invention Bdur,>Fritz Jöde, Die Kunst Bachs, dargestellt an seinen Inventionen (Wolfenbüttel: Kallmeyer, 1926), the first chapter of which is devoted to the B major Invention. Bild.

9. Studien zum Genauesten hin angesetzt: Wieder-
-holung der Berçeuse u. Walzer Asdur.
14. Das Bild einer anderen Invention korrigiert.
16. Betrachtung der Themen in der Hohen Messe.
19. Brahms Bild zuende, Fingersatz u. Vortrag.
23. Bemerkungen zur Hohen Messe beendet.
26. Erläuterungen zum Buxbaum-Abend vom 25.: Beethoven op. 97 u. Schubert Dmoll.

28. Zum Vortrag der Hohen Messe, nach dem Konzert der Berliner Singakademie unter Schumann.Diary October 27: “In the evening, Mass in B minor, performed by the Berlin Choral Society under Schumann. A carefully nuanced performance, the chorus performing to its limits, in particular the sopranos in best voice. The extent to which this type of performance can be traced back to Schumann's predecessors, perhaps even as far back as Zelter, is not known to me; in any event most of the choral movements were worthy of praise, at most one could have wanted a more differentiated working through in the Kyrie. On the other hand, the arias disappointed, as always, lacking in all care: they lacked a precise agreement between the obbligato wind or string instrument and the voices, the clarification of the form and the modulations, and much else.”
30. Bild der Chopin-Etude op. 25 No 11, Am.
4. XI. Eine Aufgabe aus „Wie bist du, meine Königin“; über das Steckel-Quartett u. das eingesandte Hindemith-Quartett.

11. Korrektur des Bildes vom Thema der Eroica-Variationen op. 35; in die Wiederholung aufgenommen: Walzer Cism, Mazurka Asdur u. Gm.Diary November 11: “Work on the B-minor Etude, Op. 25, No. 10 (for Miss Elias).”

16. Linie zu Chopin Hm-Etude
op. 25 No 10, von mir vorher angegeben.

18. Ueber die Matthäus-Passion in Furtwänglers Aufführung.Performance in the Great Hall of the Musikverein Building, November 17, Gesellschaft der Musikfreunde regular concert, under Wilhelm Furtwängler, St Matthew Passion. — Diary November 9: “Miss Elias brings tickets to the final rehearsal of the St. Matthew Passion (8 shillings).”
20. Haydn Fantasie Cdur gelesen.
23. Fingersatz zur Hm-Etude.

2. XII. Zum Forellen-Quintett; über Meirecker u. van Berg,Diary November 29: “Buxbaum Quartet (with Meirecker), program: Schubert, Op. 161 in G major, the "Trout" Quintet, and the Quartet Movement in C minor (posthumous). [...] We look for Miss Elias in the gallery; I cancel tomorrow's lesson so that I can look at the collection.” über die Henrici-Sammlung.
4. Blick in das Capriccio von Haydn.
14. Etude Hm zuende.

16. Die fragliche Stelle aus Beethovens IV. Sinfonie (s. Albersheim).Cf. Albersheim lesson for November 29: “concerning a passage in Beethoven’s Fourth Symphony, first movement: B-sharp–C-sharp or B-natural–C-sharp.” Schenker is referring to the lower neighbor-note figure in the first violins at bar 290, towards the end of the development. The autograph score reads: d2–c2–b1–c2. So does Simrock’s 1823 edition of the score. But the old Gesamtausgabe and the Eulenburg score (edited by Max Unger) both give b1. Modern editions of the symphony, however, restore the autograph reading.

21. Ueber das Philharmonischen Konzert mit Weingartners op. 106, Egmont Ouvertüre u. die V. Sinfonie.Weingarten had made an orchestration of Beethoven’s String Quartet, Op. 106. – Schenker’s diary entry for December 19 has a lengthy description of this concert, which begins: “In the Philharmonic concert: Egmont Overture: all upbeats comprising three eighth-notes not played as upbeats – without striving towards a goal tone. As a result, the overture lost all its life, all its fire. Opus 106: in itself an inexcusable error, which demonstrates that Weingartner is not aware of the difference between a piano and orchestra, nor of the difference between writing for piano and for orchestra. [...]” — Diary December 19: “Work on Chopin's last Etude (for Miss Elias).”

23. Partitur zu op. 106 angesehen.This probably refers to the score of Beethoven’s “Hammerklavier” Sonata Op. 106 in Felix Weingartner’s orchestration: cf. lessonbook entry of December 21 and footnote.
28. Bild zur Etude Cm op. 25 No 12, treffend.

4. I. Etude Cm gespielt; Arie der Königin der Nacht aus der Zauberflöte gezeigt (s. Albersheim).Cf. Albersheim’s lesson for January 3: “The Queen of the Night’s aria from The Magic Flute: the coloratura completely underpinned by the voice-leading.”
8. Berçeuse wiederholt.
15. Haydn Capriccio.

18. Bemerkungen zum Furtwängler Konzert;Concert on January 15 in the Great Hall of the Musikverein, Vienna Philharmonic under Wilhem Furtwängler, program: Mendelssohn Symphony No. 3 (“Scottish”) and Brahms Symphony No. 2 in D major. — Diary January 28: “Elias has influenza.” Paganini-Variationen neu.
10. II. Bild des Basses in Haydns Capriccio.
15. Stücke aus dem Repertoire in Frau Pairamalls Gramophon angehört.
17. Ueber Gräser u. die Neuausgabe; Bilder zu den Paganini-Variationen.
26. Nocturne Esd op. 9 wiederholt.
1. III. Ueber das Konzert Bakhaus.
17. Aus Scarlatti-Brahms Heft 6 gezeigt.
5. IV. Klein‘s Metamorphosen vorgespielt.Diary April 5: “From Heinrich Fritz Klein, Linz, Metamorphoses on themes by Beethoven.”
7. Bilder zu den Paganini Variationen abgeschlossen.
14. Unerledigte Aufgaben aus früherer Zeit in Bildern; Brahms Gm-Quartett, Modulation im 1. Satz usw.

21. Aus der Hohen Messe: Einleitung zur Ddur-Arie im Bild;Probably the soprano duet “Christe eleison,” for which there are sketches and a fair copy of a graph in Elias’s hand (OC 81/4). einige Schubert-Walzer.
26. Aus Halm’s Buch;August Halm, Beethoven (Berlin: Max Hesse, 1927), which Schenker had just received from the publisher. Nachträge zur Nocturne Esd.

28. Bild
zum Cism-Walzer korrigiert; Korrekturen zur Appassionata (nach der von ihr geschenkten Handschrift) gezeigt.Diary April 28: “Miss Elias presents me with the original edition of Haydn, in twelve volumes.” — Diary March 10: “Miss Elias brings the facsimile edition of the "Appassionata," which she chanced to see in the window of the Perles bookshop.” Cf. Diary April 23–25: “Now I begin the correction of the "Appassionata" against the autograph facsimile.” – “Correction of the "Appassionata" completed.” – “To UE, the corrections to Op. 57 sent off.”
3. V. Paganini-Variationen als Ganzes wiederholt.
10. Vierhändig die Sinfonie von Haydn aus Bd III, s. Vrieslander.
12. Impromptu Fisd, neu, Bilder.
26. Fingersatz.Diary May 26: “In spite of the holiday, I will be teaching on June May 30: Brünauer, Elias, Pairamall.” – May 30,1927 was the Monday following Ascension Day.
28. Haydn Sonate Gd gelesen, Peters I, No 10 damit verglichen.
31. Vortrag des Impromptus.
7. VI. Vortrag des Impromptus ganz.
8. Schumann: vierhändige Original-Kompositionen.Diary June 8: “Three make-up lessons given (Elias, Hoboken).”
9. Brahms „Auf dem Kirchhof“, Bild korrigiert.Diary June 10: “Urlinie for Mendelssohn's "Spring Song" (for Brünauer) and for Chopin's Prelude in D major (for Elias).”
11. Wiederholt: Prélude Desd, Hm.
18. Bild zum Prélude Desd.
22. Vierhändig Streichquartett von Haydn Cd, op. 74; Brahms 1. Sinfonie, 1. u. 3. Satz.

tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Angi Elias in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab: October 4: Brahms Op. 119, No. 1, voice-leading line begun.
October 7: Jöde; Invention in B major, graph.

October 9: Studies in the most precise way initiated:
revisiting of the Berceuse and the Waltz in A major.
October 14: The graph of a different invention corrected.
October 16: Consideration of the themes in the Mass in B minor.
October 23: Observations on the Mass in B minor finished.
October 26: Elucidations concerning the Buxbaum evening of the 25th: Beethoven Op. 97 and Schubert D minor.
October 28: On the performance of the Mass in B minor, after the concert given by the Berlin Choral Society directed by Schumann.
October 30: Graph of Chopin’s Etude in A minor, Op. 25, No. 11.
November 4: An assignment from Brahms’s song “Wie bist du, meine Königin”; concerning the Steckel Quartet and the quartet by Hindemith which was sent to me.
November 11: Correction of the graph of the theme of the “Eroica” Variations, Op. 35; taken up in repetition: Waltz in C minor, Mazurkas in A major and G minor.

November 16: Voice-leading line of Chopin’s Etude in B minor,
Op. 25, No. 10, previously indicated by me.
November 18: On the St. Matthew Passion, in Furtwängler’s performance.
November 20: Haydn’s Fantasy in C major read.
November 23: Fingering for the Etude in B minor.
December 2: On the “Trout” Quintet; concerning Meirecker and van den Berg, concerning the Henrici collection.
December 4: Glimpse of Haydn’s Capriccio.
December 14: Etude in B minor finished.
December 16: Die questionable passage from Beethoven’s Fourth Symphony (cf. Albersheim).
December 21: Concerning the Philharmonic concert with Weingartner’s Op. 106, “Egmont” Overture, and Fifth Symphony.
December 23: The score of Op. 106 examined.
December 28: Graph of the Etude in C minor, Op. 25, No. 12, to the point.
January 4: Etude in C minor played; I show her the Queen of the Night’s aria from The Magic Flute (cf. Albersheim).
January 8: Berceuse revisited.
January 15: Haydn’s Capriccio.
February 10: Graph of the bass line in Haydn’s Capriccio.
February 15: Pieces from Mrs. Pairamall’s phonograph record library listened to.
February 17: Concerning Graeser and his new edition; graphs for the Paganini Variations.
February 26: The Nocturne in E major from Op. 9 revisited.
March 1: On the Backhaus concert.
March 17: I show her things from Scarlatti–Brahms, volume 6.
April 5: I play to her Klein’s Metamorphosen.
April 7: Graphs for the Paganini Variations completed.
April 14: Unfinished assignments from an earlier time, in graphs; Brahms Quartet in G minor, modulation in the first movement, etc.
April 21: From the Mass in B minor: the introduction to the Aria in D major, graphed; some Schubert waltzes.
April 26: From Halm’s book; additional remarks on the Nocturne in E major.

April 28: Graph
of the C minor Waltz corrected; I show her corrections to the “Appassionata” (according to the facsimile edition of the manuscript she gave me).
May 3: Paganini Variations revisited, as an entire work.
May 10: The Haydn symphony from vol. III played four-hands, cf. Vrieslander.
May 12: Impromptu in F major, new; graphs.
May 26: Fingering.
May 28: Haydn’s Sonata in G major read; Peters edition, vol. I, No. 10, compared with it.
May 31: Performance of the Impromptu.
June 7: Performance of the Impromptu complete.
June 8: Schumann: original compositions for piano duet.
June 9: Brahms’s “Auf dem Kirchhof”, graph corrected.
June 11: Revisited: the preludes in D major and B minor.
June 18: Graph of the Prelude in D major.
June 22: Played four-hands: Haydn String Quartet in C major, Op. 74, and Brahms First Symphony, first and third movements.

tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Anthony van Hoboken in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab:
1. X. Dreist. Satz, 5. Gattung; Jakob
Fischers Aufsatz.Jacob Fischer, Erläuterungen zur Interpunktionsausgabe (Berlin-Lichterfelde: Schlesinger’sche Buch- & Musikhandlung, 1926). See OC 45/2 for a copy with markings.

5. Jöde Invention Bdur.Fritz Jöde, Die Kunst Bachs, dargestellt an seinen Inventionen (Wolfenbüttel: Kallmeyer, 1926). The first chapter is devoted to the Invention in B major: Der rhythmisch-dynamische Pendelschlag (Invention No. 14 B-dur), pp. 15–50. Diary Oct 15: “Hoboken said that ‘the way of viewing the Invention in B major shows the contrast between Jöde and myself: that interested me greatly. First, I would like to learn many pieces in order to gain the correct perspective; then I can indeed work in much greater detail – if I stick to it.’”

8. Fragen der Metrik nach Wiehmayer.Theodor Wiehmayer, Über die Grundfragen der musikalischen Rhythmik und Metrik, Sonderdruck aus dem Bericht über den Musikwissenschaftlichen Kongress zu Leipzig vom 4.–8. Juni 1925 (Leipzig: Breitkopf & Härtel, [1925]). See OC 45/4 for a copy with markings, and OC 45/5 for another work by Wiehmayer.

12. Metrik nach Marpurg, FischerJacob Fischer, Erläuterungen zur Interpunktionsausgabe (Berlin-Lichterfelde: Schlesinger’sche Buch- & Musikhandlung), 1926). See OC 45/2 for a copy with markings. in seinen Beispielen, dazu aus der Deklamation im Requiem von Brahms; Bemerkungen zum Rosé-Abend:Concert in the middle recital hall of the Vienna Konzerthaus: Rosé String Quartet: Beethoven Op. 18, No. 1, in F major; Op. 127 in E major; Op. 59, No. 2, in E minor. Beethoven Streichquartett op. 18 No 1 u. Esd op 127 u. op. 59 No 2.

15. Zu Beethovens op. 18 No 2 u. 59 No 1; Bach Sarabande nach meiner VorlageHeinrich Schenker, Joh. Seb. Bach: Suite III C-dur für Violoncello-Solo, Sarabande, Meisterwerk II (1926), 97–104 (Eng. transl., vol. II, pp. 55–58). zuende geführt. Zurück zur Metrik.
19. Unechte Jugendarbeiten von Beethoven; Fragen der Metrik; Hohe Messe.

22. Zur Beethoven-Sinfonie No 1 (Dirk Fock);Dirk Fock (Foch) (1886–1973), Dutch conductor, first conductor of the Vienna Konzertverein orchestra in the 1920s and 1930s; he briefly directed orchestral rehearsals at the Vienna Conservatory in 1924; cf. Diary March 20, 2026: “Van Hoboken brings Stravinsky's concerto and a few remarks by Fock in the program booklet. I shall keep the concerto at my place for a while.” Hohe Messe zuende.Diary Oct 22: “Hoboken [...] regarding the preparation for [the performance of] the Mass in B minor, I postpone a discussion as I have a meeting.”

26. Zum Buxbaum-Abend. op. 97 u. Schubert Dm;Cf. Elias lesson for same day: “Elucidations concerning the Buxbaum evening of the 25th: Beethoven’s Op. 97 and Schubert’s Quartet in D minor.” aus Bruckners V. Sinfonie ein paar Stellen.
29. Aus Bruckners III. Sinfonie; Hohe Messe: Vortragsfragen durchgesprochen, Programm des Jahres festgestellt.
2. XI. Hindemith-Quartett; Brahms „Wie bist du meine Königin“; Brahms IV. Sinfonie, 1. Satz ganz.

5. Brahms IV. Sinfonie 2., 3. u. 4. Satz (!!!). Erzählt, Specht bei Zsolnay entgegengetreten zu sein, der die Urlinie ablehnt.Diary Nov 5: “Hoboken recounts that, at the home of Zsolnay's father, he met Mr. Specht, who yapped a bit against me: that I am spoiling the younger generation, promulgating the Urlinie in which he does not believe, and the like.”

8. Clementi Am No 17, neu; schreibt die Urlinie des Themas der Eroica Variationen; über Beethovens Fd-Variationen op. 34.Diary Nov 7: “In the morning, work on Clementi's Gradus ad Parnassum (looked through four etudes for Hoboken from the perspective of a line).”
16. Stellt die Frage: Brahms Klavier-Quartett Gm, Modulationspartie.

19. Mischungen mit der 5. Gattung; Chopin Nocturne Esdur op. 9 No 2 neu, Ursatz; über die Matthäuspassion (Furtwängler).Performance in the Great Hall of the Musikverein Building, November 17, Gesellschaft der Musikfreunde regular concert, under Wilhelm Furtwängler, St Matthew Passion. The concert was discussed also in Elias’s lesson for November 18.
23. Vortrag der Nocturne.
26. Ueber einige Lanner-Walzer u. ihre Urlinie.Diary Nov 24: “In waltzes by Lanner, the Urlinie likewise ascertained.” Cf. Diary Oct 13: “At Gutmann's I order [...] waltzes by Lanner.”

30. Die fragliche Stelle in Beethovens IV. Sinfonie;In the passage in question (first movement, bar 290, first-violin part), which was also discussed at Albersheim’s lesson on November 29 and again at Elias’s on December 16, Beethoven’s autograph score reads: d2–c2–b1–c2, as does Simrock’s 1823 edition of the score. The old Gesamtausgabe and the Eulenburg score (edited by Max Unger) both give b1. Modern editions of the symphony, however, restore the autograph reading. über das Forellen-Quintett als Komposition; – Stellen aus Mozarts Klavier-Violin-Sonate
Bd.; Clementi–Tausig Cd.;Diary Nov 28: “Before lunch, more work on the fugue of the "Eroica" Variations, Clementi C-major Etude (for Hoboken).” bringt den Erstdruck vom Paganini-Thema, das den Brahms- u. Liszt-Variationen zu Grunde liegt.

7. XII. Eine selbst verfertigte Linie zu Telemanns Bourrée (Cotta); zeigt Lanner-Bearbeitungen von Gál, eine Londoner Ausgabe von Scarlatti, einiges darin unbekannt; zeige Roth’s 1. Heft des Kontrapunkts.Herman Roth, Elemente der Stimmführung (Stuttgart: J. G. Cotta, 1926).

10. Chopin Nocturne gründlich im Vortrag durchgearbeitet; Clementi Cd-Etude für die l. H., neu; zeige einen Brief von Dr Einstein.Perhaps OC 54/109, written on behalf of the publisher of Das Meisterwerk, Drei Masken Verlag, though that is dated December 11. — Diary Dec 14–15: “I show van H. the letter from Einstein – he is opposed to court action; the Yearbook must be out by October 27 at the latest, that remains the most important thing.” – “To Vrieslander (letter): concerning yesterday's conversation with van H.”

21. Ueber Weingartners op. 106 u. die anderen Stücke des Philharmonischen Konzertes;Schenker’s diary entry for December 19 gives a lengthy description of this concert, which begins: “In the Philharmonic concert: “Egmont” Overture: all upbeats comprising three eighth-notes not played as upbeats – without striving towards a goal tone. As a result, the overture lost all its life, all its fire. Opus 106: in itself an inexcusable error, which demonstrates that Weingartner is not aware of the difference between a piano and an orchestra, nor of the difference between writing for piano and for orchestra.” neu Clementi Cd, Brechungen.

28. Brahms Fingerübungen, einige neu; zeige in Paganinis Erstdruck die verteilte Baßführung gegen Ende; Scarlatti Sonate Dm, neu (Volksausgabe No 1): Linie, Fingersatz,
Vortrag.

31. Bringt die Urlinie der Nocturne Fisd (aus Eigenem), recht gut.Diary Dec 31: “Hoboken raises his payment for lessons to 6 dollars and pays six months in advance; he presents the Urlinie of the Nocturne, which he prepared by himself!”
4. I. Sämtliche bisher gespielten Etüden von Clementi wiederholt; Coloratur-Arie der Königin der Nacht aus der Zauberflöte.[Schenker had Albersheim and Elias working on this aria at the same time.

7. II. Ueber die Fehler in Vrieslanders Reinschrift; über meine Absage an Prof. Adler;On January 28, Adler invited Schenker to deliver a paper at the Beethoven Centennial Celebration (OJ 9/3, [5]), which Schenker declined on February 7 (OJ 5/3, [1]). Though the month is not specified, it is clear from the evidence in the diary (including January 4: “Hoboken announces a four-week holiday”) and several items of correspondence that Hoboken had only one lesson in January, which took place on the 4th. gehen das 2. Heft Brahms–ScarlattiBrahms owned several volumes of manuscript copies of Scarlatti’s keyboard sonatas, which he bequeathed to the Gesellschaft der Musikfreunde in Vienna. See Elizabeth McKay, Brahms and Scarlatti, Musical Times 130 (1989), pp. 586–88. durch; über Gräsers „Kunst der Fuge.“Gräser’s published orchestration of Bach’s Art of Fugue (first performed in Leipzig on June 26, 1927, as mentioned in Schenker’s diary for July 2); he also discussed this with Elias on February 17. It is mentioned several times in the diary between mid-January and July 2.

15. Ueber die „Ehrenzeichen-Frage“;Diary Feb 15: “Section Head Kobald intends to recommend me for an honor in the Ministry for Education”; Feb 26: “From Floriz Moriz Violin (letter): he understands that I am turning down the honor and indicates a way of thinking that I should advance in order to justify turning it down”; Schenker enumerates reasons for declining in OJ 5/9, [1], February 28, 1927. er erzählt, daß Vrieslander über mich schreibt; Clementi Fism Etude,Diary Feb 16: “I work on Clementi's Etude in F minor (for Hoboken).” neu; vierstimm. Satz, 1. u. 2. Gattung; zur VI. Sinfonie von Beethoven, Andante.

22. Clementi Ad No 9,Diary Feb 20: “I work on Clementi [Etudes] Nos. 9, 10, 11 (for Hoboken).” neu, dazu Tausig; Brahms–Scarlatti 3. HeftBrahms owned several volumes of manuscript copies of Scarlatti’s keyboard sonatas, which he bequeathed to the Gesellschaft der Musikfreunde in Vienna. See Elizabeth McKay, Brahms and Scarlatti, Musical Times 130 (1989), pp. 586–88. durchgegangen.Diary Feb 22: “Hoboken shows me a letter from Vrieslander, which is in agreement with the one sent to me; [...] Brahms-Scarlatti, [vol.] 3, returned.”
25. Hat die Nocturne Esd auswendig gespielt geschrieben!! Bild des Basses zu Scarlatti Clementi Ad; Chopin Nocturne Fisd, Vortrag.

1. III. Ueber das Backhaus Konzert;Discussed also in Elias’s lesson for the same day. Scarlatti 4. u. 5. HeftBrahms owned several volumes of manuscript copies of Scarlatti’s keyboard sonatas, which he bequeathed to the Gesellschaft der Musikfreunde in Vienna. See Elizabeth McKay, Brahms and Scarlatti, Musical Times 130 (1989), pp. 586–88. durchgegangen.

8. Aus Eigenem die Urlinie zu Scarlatti Fd, sehr gut.Diary March 8: “Hoboken surprises me with successfully written-out Urlinie graph of Scarlatti's Sonata in F major, made on his own initiative! It is clear how, with good will, even such an assignment can meet with success when one is not tainted or inhibited by vanity.” Entwurf einer Stiftung.This is the first mention of a bequest that would support the foundation of the Photogram Archive of autograph manuscripts of master composers. Bringt die Gräser-AusgabeWolfgang Graeser’s orchestration of J. S. Bach’s Kunst der Fuge. Cf. lesson for February 7, above. u. Stücke von Debussy.
11. Skizzen zu op. 106, von Hecks zugeschickt.
15. Clementi opNo. 11, neu.Diary March 15: “I work on the Urlinie for Clementi's Etude No. 11 in A major (for Hoboken).”

18. Scarlatti–BrahmsBrahms owned several volumes of manuscript copies of Scarlatti’s keyboard sonatas, which he bequeathed to the Gesellschaft der Musikfreunde in Vienna. See Elizabeth McKay, Brahms and Scarlatti, Musical Times 130 (1989), pp. 586–88. 6. u. 7. Heft.Diary March 18: “Hoboken brings the sketch for "Chaos" Haydn, Creation once more.”

22. Bringt Vrieslander mit, dann alle zum Konzert Dirk Schäfer.Concert in the middle recital hall of the Vienna Konzerthaus: Beethoven Centenary Celebration by Dirk Schäfer, program: Diabelli Variations, op. 120, “Moonlight” Sonata.
25. Vrieslander in Hob. Stunde; macht mit mir die Korrekturen.

29. 8. Heft.Brahms owned several volumes of manuscript copies of Scarlatti’s keyboard sonatas, which he bequeathed to the Gesellschaft der Musikfreunde in Vienna. See Elizabeth McKay, Brahms and Scarlatti, Musical Times 130 (1989), pp. 586–88.
1. IV. Weitere Hefte von Scarlatti.

5. Klein’s Metamorphosen gezeigt,Diary April 5: “From Heinrich Fritz Klein, Linz, Metamorphoses on themes by Beethoven.” Klenau’s Lästerschule;Diary April 2: “[Klenau] explains that he has written his new opera, Die Lästerschule, in the spirit of Mozart, mainly with simple cadences. I reply that Mozart's simplicity is by no means so simple; Klenau will send the piano-vocal score.” Scarlatti weitere Hefte.
8.–22. Scarlatti-Hefte.Diary April 12: “Hoboken takes his Scarlatti volumes (all of them!) home, brings the first and second “Leonora” overtures.”

3. V. Ueber die Handschrift der Appassionata; die Ungenauigkeit einer diplomatischen Wiedergabe im Urtext; über die Leonoren-Ouvertüren 2. u. 3.
neue Studien aus Brahms; über das Ueben im Allgemeinen: allerdings im Anfang sehr langsam, doch muß die letzte Schnelligkeit von vornherein angelegt sein.

6. Scarlatti-Hefte zuende. Spiele vor:Diary May 6: “With Hoboken, Scarlatti–Brahms brought to conclusion; he is away on travels until the 24th.” (Brahms owned several volumes of manuscript copies of Scarlatti’s keyboard sonatas, which he bequeathed to the Gesellschaft der Musikfreunde in Vienna. See Elizabeth McKay, Brahms and Scarlatti, Musical Times 130 (1989), pp. 586–88.) aus Mendelssohns Fugensammlung op. 35 die Fuge Dd, Gondellied Ad.None of Mendelssohn’s three Venetian Boat Songs (Gondellieder) is in the key of A major; Schenker may be referring to Op. 62, No. 5, which is in A minor but ends in A major.

27. Zeigt ein Verzeichnis von Pariser Handschriften.Diary May 27: “Hoboken appears, bringing with him a substantial index of autograph manuscripts that are housed in the Paris library – we work our way carefully through the index.”
28. Zeigt Scarlatti-Longo Ausgabe. Ueber den Unterschied einiger Stellen in Haydns Sonate Gd. in Peters I, 10 u. in der Original Ausgabe. Stellen aus Brahms’ I. Sinfonie.
7. VI. Bringt ein Heft der „Musik"Die Musik, xix/9. mit neuen Händel-Funden.

8. Ueber diese Stücke, namentlich das Presto der Suite Dm u. das Menuett in Cm, das ich Bach zuschreibe. Schumann: Bilder aus dem Osten, vierhändig.Diary June 8: “Three make-up lessons given (Elias, Hoboken).”

10. Sämtliche Cle-
-menti-Etüden wiederholt.

14. Zur Fisd-Nocturne einiges aus der Literatur: GalstonPossibly the chapter on Chopin from Galston’s Studienbuch (Berlin: Bruno Cassirer, 1910). u. Klindworth.Possibly the six-volume edition of Chopin’s works, first published by Jurgenson (Moscow, 1873–76) and later reissued in Berlin and London. Original-Fingersatz von Brahms in op. 116 No 1. Aus Mozarts Streichquartetten nach Albersheims Fragestellung.

17. Weitere Original-Fingersätze von Brahms in den Klavierstücken op. 76–119. Zeigt von Haydn ein eigenes Verzeichnis seiner Werke.This was the earliest stage of what became Joseph Haydn: Thematisch-bibliographisches Werkverzeichnis (Mainz: Schott, 1957–78), which began with the assistance of Otto Erich Deutsch, Hoboken’s private librarian.

22. Konferenz mit Doz. Dr. Haas.Diary June 22: “At 4:30 Hoboken, with whom I go through the correction of his circular; at 5 o'clock, docent Haas – until 6:45: the first meeting of the Board of Trustees, so to speak!” (Schenker is referring here to what would soon become the Photogram Archive of the Austrian National Library.)

tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Anthony van Hoboken in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab:
October 1: Three-voice counterpoint, fifth species; Jakob
Fischer’s essay.
October 5: Jöde, Invention in B major.
October 8: Questions about metrical matters, according to Wiehmayer.

October 12: Metrical matters according to Marpurg and Fischer in his examples; in addition, remarks on declamation in Brahms’s German Requiem; observations on the Rosé evening: Beethoven String Quartet Op. 18, No. 1, Op. 127 in E, and Op. 59, No. 2.
October 15: On Beethoven’s Op. 18, No. 2, and Op. 59, No. 1; Bach’s Sarabande, in accordance with my model, brought to an end. Back to metrical matters.
October 19: Spurious juvenilia of Beethoven’s; questions about meter; Mass in B minor.
October 26: On the Buxbaum evening: Op. 97 and Schubert’s Quartet in D minor. A few passages from Bruckner’s Fifth Symphony.
October 29:On Bruckner’s Third Symphony; Mass in B minor: questions about performance thoroughly discussed; program for the year determined.
November 2: Hindemith’s quartet; Brahms “Wie bist du meine Königin”; Brahms Fourth Symphony, first movement in its entirety.
November 5: Brahms Fourth Symphony, second, third and fourth movements (!!!). He tells me that he met Specht at Zsolnay’s, who rejects the Urlinie.
November 8: Clementi No. 17 in A minor, new; he writes out the Urlinie of the theme of the “Eroica” Variations; concerning Beethoven’s Variations in F major, Op. 34.
November 16: He asks the question about the modulatory section in Brahms’s Piano Quartet in G minor.
November 19: Mixed-species counterpoint in the fifth species; Chopin Nocturne in E major, Op. 9 No. 2, new, Ursatz; On the St. Matthew Passion (Furtwängler).
November 23: Performance of the Nocturne.
November 26: Concerning a few waltzes by Lanner, and their Urlinie.

November 30: The questionable passage in Beethoven’s Fourth Symphony; on the “Trout” Quintet as a composition; – Passages from Mozart’s Sonata in B for Piano and Violin.
Clementi–Tausig in C major; he brings the first edition of the Paganini theme, upon which the variations by Brahms and Liszt are based.

December 7: A voice-leading line for Telemann’s Bourrée (published by Cotta), made on his own; He shows me Gál’s arrangements of Lanner, a London edition of Scarlatti, in which some sonatas were unknown to me; I show him the first volume of Roth’s counterpoint study.
December 10: Chopin Nocturne thoroughly worked out in performance; Clementi’s C major Etude for the left hand, new; I show him a letter from Dr. Einstein.
December 21: On Weingartner’s orchestration of Op. 106 and the other works played at the Philharmonic concert; new: Clementi C major, arpeggiations.

December 28: Brahms’s finger exercises, some of which are new; in the Paganini first edition, I show him the divided voice-leading in the bass towards the end. Scarlatti Sonata in D minor, new (Volksausgabe No. 1): voice-leading line, fingering,
performance.
December 31: He brings the Urlinie of the Nocturne in F major (on his own initiative), very good.
January 4: All the previously played Clementi etudes revisited; The Queen of the Night’s coloratura aria from The Magic Flute.

February 7: Concerning the mistakes in Vrieslander’s fair copy; concerning my letter of rejection to Professor Adler; we go through the second volume of Brahms–Scarlatti; concerning Gräser’s Art of Fugue.

February 15: Concerning the matter of conferring an honor; he tells me that Vrieslander is writing about me; Clementi F minor Etude, new; four-voice counterpoint in first and second species; on the Andante of Beethoven’s Sixth Symphony.
February 22: Clementi No. 9 in A major, new, also Tausig; Brahms–Scarlatti volume 3 examined.
February 25: He has played written out the Nocturne in E major from memory!! Graph of the bass line of Scarlatti Clementi’s Etude in A major; Chopin Nocturne in F major, performance.
March 8: On his own initiative, the Urlinie of Scarlatti’s F major, very good. Draft of a bequest. He brings Gräser’s edition and pieces by Debussy.
March 11: Sketches for Op. 106, sent by Heck.
March 15: Clementi Etude No. 11, new.
March 18: Scarlatti–Brahms volumes 6 and 7.
March 22: He brings Vrieslander with him, then we all go to Dirk Schäfer’s concert.
March 25: Vrieslander at Hoboken’s lesson; he makes the corrections with me.
March 29: Volume 8 of Brahms–Scarlatti.
April 1: Further volumes of Scarlatti.
April 5: Klein’s Metamorphosen shown, Klenau’s Die Lästerschule; further volumes of Scarlatti.
April 8–22: Scarlatti volumes.

May 3: Concerning the autograph manuscript of the “Appassionata”; the imprecision of a diplomatic transcription in the Urtext; concerning “Leonora” Overtures No. 2. and No. 3.
new studies from Brahms. Concerning practice in general: very slow at the beginning, in all cases; but the ultimate speed must be established at the outset.
May 6: Scarlatti volumes finished. I play to him the fugue in D major from Mendelssohn’s collection of fugues Op. 35, and the Venetian Boat Song in A major.
May 27: He shows me an index of autograph manuscripts in Paris.

May 28: He shows me Longo’s edition of Scarlatti. Concerning the difference of some passages in the original edition and Peter’s edition (vol. I, No. 10) of Haydn’s Sonata in G major. Passages from Brahms’s First Symphony.
June 7: He brings a volume of Die Musik with new Handel discoveries.
June 8: Concerning these pieces by Handel, especially the Presto from the Suite in D minor, and the Minuet in C minor, which I would ascribe to Bach. Schumann: Pictures from the Orient, four-hands.

June 10: All the
Clementi Etudes revisited.

June 14: A few things about the F major Nocturne from the literature: Galston and Klindworth. Brahms’s original fingering in his Op. 116, No. 1. Matters concerning Mozart’s string quartets, based on questions asked by Albersheim.
June 17: Further examples of Brahms’s original fingering in the piano pieces Opp. 76–119. He shows me a catalog of his own of Haydn’s works.
June 22: Meeting with the docent, Dr. Haas.

tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Marianne Kahn in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab: 2. X. Beethoven op. 31 No 1 wiederholt. Bach-Brahms Chaconne für die linke Hand, neu.
15. Beethoven Sonate op. 31 No 2 wiederholt.
6. XI. Beethoven Gd-Konzert, schon vor vielen Jahren gespielt, doch wie neu; 1. u. 2. Satz; Berçeuse wiederholt.

20. Chopin Impromptu CismProbably the Fantasy-Impromptu in C minor, Op. 66, intended for Kahn’s pupils. (für Schüler); Brahms Capriccio Hm, neu; Beethoven
Konzert, letzter Satz.
4. XII. Beethoven Sonate Fd, op. 10 No 2 wiederholt; Chopin Nocturne Esd. op. 9 No 2, Asd. neu.

18. op. 32 No 3There is no No. 3 in Chopin’s Nocturnes Op. 32; Schenker may mean Op. 32, No. 2, in A major. Or he may mean Beethoven’s Sonata in E major, Op. 31, No. 3, as Kahn had been working on Nos. 1 and 2 in October. wiederholt; Walzer Asd u. Desd; Berçeuse, besonders Anfang.Diary December 18: “I offer to teach Miss Kahn free of charge; she declines, expressing her gratitude.” – December 31: “To Mrs. Kaposi and Miss Kahn (express postcard): postponement of the lessons.”
8. I. Etüden op. 25, das 1. Heft.
19. Sonate Cism u. Fm wiederholt.
19. Pathetique.
2. IV. op. 53 zuende; – wiederholt Nocturne Bm op. 9, Esd, Berçeuse.
16. Nocturne Fd, Hd, Esd.

7. V. Nocturne Fisd, Hd, Fm; Schubert Impromptu Asd 3/4, neu (für Schüler); Schubert Gd Impromptu wiederholt.This work, originally written in G major, was more widely known in the early 20th century in transposition up a semitone.
21. Brahms-Paganini, beide Hefte wiederholt.
9. VI. Beethoven Sonate op. 81a, neu, alle Sätze; S. Bachs 1. Cm-Fuge wiederholt.
18. VI. Brahms-Händel-Var. wiederholt.

tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Marianne Kahn in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab: October 2: Beethoven Op. 31, No. 1, revisited. Bach-Brahms Chaconne for the left hand, new.
October 15: Beethoven Sonata Op. 31, No. 2, revisited.
November 6: Beethoven G major Concerto, already played many years earlier, yet as if new, first and second movements; Berceuse revisited.

November 20: Chopin Impromptu in C minor (for her pupils); Brahms Capriccio in B minor, new; Beethoven
Concerto, last movement.
December 4: Beethoven Sonata in F major, Op. 10, No. 2, revisited; Chopin Nocturne in E major Op. 9, No. 2, A major new.
January 8: Etudes Op. 25, the first volume.
January 22: Op. 110 and Op. 111.
February 4: Op. 109 and Op. 101.
February 19: Sonatas in C minor and F minor revisited.
March 5: Op. 106.
March 19: “Pathétique” Sonata.
April 2: Op. 53 to the end; revisited: Nocturnes Op. 9: No. 1 in B minor and No. 2 in E major, and the Berceuse.
April 16: Nocturnes in F major, B major, and E major.
May 7: Nocturnes in F major, B major, and F minor; Schubert Impromptu in A major, 3/4 time, new (for her pupils); Schubert G major Impromptu revisited.
May 21: Brahms-Paganini, both volumes revisited.
June 9: Beethoven, Sonata Op. 81a, new, all movements; J. S. Bach’s Fugue in C minor from Book I revisited.
June 18: Brahms’s Handel Variations revisited.

tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Georg Schenker in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab: 22. XII. Appassionata 1. Satz wiederholt;– op. 81a begonnen.Diary November 26: “From 6:45 to 8:30 Mr. und Mrs. Kaposi: the wife asks to have lessons, I make space for these every second and fourth Saturday.”
15. I. op.81a 1. Satz zuende, Appassionata 2. Satz wiederholt.
29. op.81a 2. Satz.
26. II. op. 81a, letzter Satz; wiederholt Brahms’ Rhapsodie,Probably the Rhapsody in B minor, Op. 79, No. 1, which Schenker taught frequently. Intermezzo Cd op. 118 119 , No 3.
11. VI. Chopin Scherzo Bm, neu.
25. Chopin Scherzo zuende.Diary June 22: “Make-up lessons: Mrs. Kaposi, to whom I announce the fee increase.”

tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Georg Schenker in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab: December 22 Appassionata, first movement revisited; – Op. 81a begun.
January 15 Op.81a, first movement finished, Appassionata, second movement revisited.
January 29 op.81a, second movement.
February 26 Op. 81a, last movement; revisiting of Brahms’s Rhapsody and Intermezzo in C major, Op. 119, No. 3.
June 11 Chopin Scherzo in B minor, new.
June 25 Chopin Scherzo finished.
Fehlt die ganze Saison.
Absent for the entire Saison.
